newsitem.title: USA: Yen fallen too far, ex-MOF official Gyohten says.
newsitem.headline: Yen fallen too far, ex-MOF official Gyohten says.

text.p: The yen has weakened too far and that is likely to lead to a widening of Japan's trade surplus, a former senior Japanese Ministry of Finance official said on Tuesday.

"The current level of the Japanese yen is excessively weak," said Toyoo Gyohten, who is now a senior advisor to the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd. "That will certainly have an impact on the Japanese trade imbalance."
Interviewed by Reuters Financial Television, Gyohten said that concern was mounting in both the United States and Japan about the trade outlook.

"This development clearly indicates the overshooting of the exchange rate," he said. "It is quite reasonable to expect they will operate in taking some measures to cope with this situation if they think the external situation is something they cannot accept," he added.

Gyohten, a former Japanese vice finance minister for international affairs, said he was disappointed by the reaction of world currency markets to Sunday's statement by the Group of Seven industrial nations.

"I thought the G7 ministers and governors sent a clear message to the market that ... a further weakening of the yen or further strengthening of the dollar would not reflect the fundamental economic conditions," Gyohten said.
He voiced hopes that any action taken by the G7 in response to developments on the currency markets would be a concerted one.

The G7 -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- warned on Sunday of the dangers of big shifts in currency rates that could hurt world trade. But the markets did not seem to listen and pushed up the dollar.
